canonical.title: Printing Longest Increasing Subsequence
canonical.sourceFilePath: 14. Dynamic Programming/7. DP on LIS/02. Print LIS.cpp

narrative.title: The Relay Route Printout
narrative.scenario: The relay planner's follow-up request: don't just count the longest handoff chain — print one. Dispatch wants the actual station tags in order so drivers can rehearse the run. When several chains tie for longest, any one of them is acceptable.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n and an array arr of n integers.
narrative.outputFormat: Return one longest strictly increasing subsequence of arr as an array of its values.

testCases.explanation: One valid length-4 chain; [2, 5, 7, 101] is equally correct.
Three rising tags; [4, 11, 16] and [5, 11, 16] both qualify.

hintLevels: Level 1: Fill the usual length table, but also remember, for each index, who its best predecessor was.
Level 2: Keep a parent array; on each improvement dp[i] = dp[prev] + 1, store parent[i] = prev.
Level 3: Start at the table maximum and follow parents backwards, then reverse the collected values.
